effort: Redirect into a planned 45-degree exit while keeping the plant and first step aligned.
brief: E2 is the diagonal running-cut task. A paused split-stance jump supplies directed push, a cut-to-stick isolates the terminal position, a crossover bound exposes crossing force acceptance, a split-step links a low landing to an exit, and a same-leg diagonal hop isolates single-leg absorption.
marker: Count E2 attempts where braking begins before the cone, the plant knee follows the foot and the first two steps remain on the 45-degree exit line; note left/right plant separately.
readiness: Confirm diagonal single-leg landing control and a clean low split-step before adding speed. Without reported response from Class 2, use modest approach intent and short flight distances.
space: The running cuts require an 8 m × 6 m cleared two-dimensional bay including run-off; this width is unconfirmed and must be measured. Mirror routes one at a time. The final 2.5 m stopping corridor continues along the exit heading, not back toward the approach.

drills.name: Paused Split-Stance Diagonal Jump
drills.execution: Hold a shallow split stance for 2 s, push diagonally forward within 0.5 m and land on both feet for a 2 s hold.
drills.job: Produce a directed first push from stillness without relying on an incoming run.
drills.layout: Clear a 3 m × 3 m landing area; mirror the lead leg and exit diagonal. No run-up.
drills.difference: Paused split-stance two-foot takeoff and shared landing; not the lateral bilateral countermovement jump or unilateral bound.
drills.regress: Shorten flight and stance if the rear leg catches up awkwardly.

drills.name: 45-Degree Cut and Reaccelerate
drills.execution: Run in 2 m, brake before the cone, cut 45 degrees and accelerate 2 m; stop within another 2.5 m.
drills.layout: Use the stated bay; mark the incoming line, 45-degree exit, end of acceleration and end of stopping. Keep the straight-ahead abort corridor empty.
drills.difference: One diagonal planted running cut, distinct from a 180-degree return or shuffle-to-forward gait change.
drills.regress: Lower approach speed if the athlete plants too far outside the body or drifts off the exit.
drills.exposure: 1 cut, 1 turn-braking phase and 1 final stop.

drills.name: 45-Degree Cut-and-Stick
drills.execution: Use a 1.5 m brisk entry, redirect through 45 degrees for 1 m and stop in a balanced staggered stance for 2 s; no sprint-out.
drills.job: Own the diagonal receiving position separately from the main drill's running exit.
drills.layout: Same bay but a separate short cone route. The 1 m outgoing leg includes its final stopping; keep a further 2 m clear beyond it.
drills.difference: Terminal control after a diagonal redirection; E2 continues accelerating instead. It is not a second copy at a different speed.
drills.regress: Shorten the entry and lower its speed if the stop needs a recovery hop.
drills.exposure: 1 direction change, approach braking and terminal stopping; no flight prescribed.

drills.name: Crossover Bound to Stick
drills.execution: From side-facing stance, cross the far leg to load it, then bound a short diagonal onto the other leg and hold 2 s. One flight only.
drills.job: Accept the diagonal force produced after the hips cross the original base.
drills.layout: One crossover ground step within 0.5 m; flight within 0.5 m in a 3 m × 3 m clear area. Record the ground step separately from flight distance.
drills.difference: A crossover loads one bounded flight and terminal single-leg landing; Class 1's crossover continues running.
drills.regress: Reduce the crossover width and bound distance if the pelvis rotates beyond control.
drills.exposure: 1 unilateral landing; one controlled ground entry step, not a sprint.

drills.name: Split-Step to Diagonal Sprint
drills.execution: Make a very low two-foot split-step, land with feet under the hips and immediately push into a known 45-degree 2 m exit; stop over 2.5 m.
drills.job: Turn a small preparatory landing into the first diagonal running step.
drills.layout: Place the stationary split-step at the cut point and use the clear diagonal exit corridor; no approach run or added hop.
drills.difference: Bilateral landing initiates the run, unlike a static start, a run-to-cut or a jump that ends in a hold.
drills.regress: Lower hop height and exit speed if the athlete sinks or adds a recovery jump.
drills.exposure: 1 low bilateral landing, one running exit and final stop; no incoming-momentum cut.

drills.name: Single-Leg Diagonal Hop to Stick
drills.execution: Hop diagonally forward no more than 0.4 m from one leg to that same leg; hold 2 s.
drills.job: Check and strengthen the rapid same-leg acceptance needed when the cut leg must support the body again.
drills.layout: 3 m × 3 m clear landing area; choose the diagonal that moves away from the free leg, then mirror.
drills.difference: Same-leg takeoff/landing; earlier diagonal jumps share the landing or switch legs.
drills.regress: Shorten the hop for toe clawing, knee drift or free-foot touchdown.

light.job: Control pelvis rotation over the planted leg before directing the diagonal exit.
Retain active foot pressure during an oblique plant.

strength.job: Lead-leg knee/hip force for the 45-degree plant and first exit.
Retain posterior hip force while the torso inclines into the new path.
Frontal acceptance supports the lateral component of the diagonal cut.
Knee-flexor support complements the hip hinge during braking.
Adductor support maintains pelvis height as force redirects diagonally.
Bent-knee ankle force supports the oblique shin position and push-off.

previous_review: Class 2 reduced locomotor exposure to six attempts while adding eight bilateral and four unilateral landings. No completed work or recovery was reported; new drill identities were checked against all twelve prior entries.
progression: Introduce direction, not entry-speed overload. The 45-degree task carries forward early braking from Classes 1–2 without repeating their drills. Keep flight doses to two attempts in each supporting task.
strength_progression: Retain the Class 2 one-round split-squat dose while introducing diagonal tasks; RDL and soleus retain two rounds and other lifts one. No load increase is prescribed without actual feedback. This avoids adding knee-dominant volume at the same time as a new cut direction.
audit: Restricted the diagonal running exit and included its continued stopping path. Distinguished same-leg, opposite-leg and bilateral landings rather than treating all as equal. Cut-to-stick remains a small terminal-control task after the primary running cut. Final sequence review retained the preceding one-round split squat rather than restoring two rounds without athlete response.
next: Next class consolidates braking with fewer directional cuts; review actual landing/plant control and strength effort before selecting demands.

light_entries.name: Hip Airplane — supported
light_entries.execution: Bodyweight, hand support and slight hip hinge. Slowly open/close pelvis through a small owned arc without rolling the stance foot.
light_entries.rest: Keep easy; rest 30 s between legs.
light_entries.regress: Reduce arc or use more hand support if knee/foot rotates uncontrollably.
light_entries.job: Control pelvis rotation over the planted leg before directing the diagonal exit.

light_entries.name: Short-Foot Drill — supported standing hold
light_entries.execution: **5 s relaxed reset** between holds, **30 s between feet**, **60 s before P1**. Stand with most weight on the working foot and fingertip support.
light_entries.regress: Strengthen active arch control while maintaining heel, big-toe base and little-toe base contact for planting. Keep toes long; do not roll onto the outside edge. Use bilateral weight support instead if arch control needs toe-clawing or ankle rolling.
light_entries.job: Retain active foot pressure during an oblique plant.

strength_entries.name: Split Squat — two dumbbells, both feet on floor
strength_entries.execution: **3 s down**, smooth forceful rise; 2–3 RIR. Rest **60 s between legs, 120 s between rounds**.
strength_entries.regress: Keep full front-foot pressure and knee travel aligned with the foot. Reduce load/range for heel lift, knee drift or trunk collapse.
strength_entries.job: Lead-leg knee/hip force for the 45-degree plant and first exit.

strength_entries.name: Romanian Deadlift — two dumbbells
strength_entries.execution: bilateral; **2 s down**, purposeful hip extension; 2–3 RIR. Rest **120 s between working sets**.
strength_entries.regress: Maintain a softly bent, nearly constant knee angle, weights close and a controlled back position; stop lowering at the owned range.
strength_entries.job: Retain posterior hip force while the torso inclines into the new path.

strength_entries.name: Lateral Lunge — goblet dumbbell
strength_entries.execution: step out, lower **2 s**, push back to the original stance; 2–3 RIR. Rest **60 s between legs**.
strength_entries.regress: Keep the lunging foot grounded and knee aligned; sit into that hip without rotating away. Reduce width, depth or load for loss of control.
strength_entries.job: Frontal acceptance supports the lateral component of the diagonal cut.

strength_entries.name: Glute Bridge Iso Hold — long-lever hamstring variant
strength_entries.execution: bilateral. Heels farther from the hips than a standard bridge, knees still bent; bodyweight or a securely hand-held sandbag over the pelvis to reach the holding-effort target.
strength_entries.regress: Try to pull the heels toward the body without sliding them; keep ribs down. Bring heels closer or remove load for cramp/lost height; stop for symptoms.
strength_entries.job: Knee-flexor support complements the hip hinge during braking.

strength_entries.name: Copenhagen Side Plank — short lever
strength_entries.execution: top knee/lower thigh on a stable bench, lower leg clear. Rest **60 s between sides**. Use bodyweight; if already controlled and too easy, secure a small dumbbell at the upper hip with the upper hand to reach the holding-effort target.
strength_entries.regress: Keep shoulder comfortable and pelvis level. Use light lower-foot assistance if needed; stop for groin/shoulder pain or loss of position.
strength_entries.alternative: If no suitable stable Copenhagen support fits, use instead floor side-lying hip adduction, upper foot on the floor in front, 1 × 8 per lower leg at 2–3 RIR with 60 s between sides; add a small hand-secured dumbbell above the inner knee only if needed and comfortable. Its preparation is 1 × 4 easy reps per leg instead of the hold ramps. This proposed replacement adds 16 dynamic working reps and removes 30 s of working holds; preparation adds 8 reps and removes 10 s of holds. Bouts are unchanged; allow up to 2 extra minutes.
strength_entries.job: Adductor support maintains pelvis height as force redirects diagonally.

strength_entries.name: Bent-Knee Soleus Raise — seated, dumbbells on thighs
strength_entries.execution: bilateral; knees near 90°, forefeet on floor, **1 s at top, 2 s lowering, quiet bottom reset**; 2–3 RIR. Rest **90 s between sets**.
strength_entries.regress: Secure the weights above the knees, maintain knee angle and repeatable heel rise. Reduce load if heel height falls or bouncing replaces muscle force.
strength_entries.alternative: For seated calf work, use a securely held sandbag instead of dumbbells when its shape and load fit better.
strength_entries.job: Bent-knee ankle force supports the oblique shin position and push-off.
